meta_reflection: 2026.06.454 was a submission-readiness capstone milestone, not an empty one: it shipped a CLEAN full-25 held-out first-win number (0.04, flag_resolved=true — the single largest GPU arm, exp4928 ~11.2 min on gpu0_cuda, is now COUNTED rather than quarantined, directly closing the .450->.452 recurring flag), confirmed the submission package ready before the 6/30 deadline, and retired the MATM efficiency lever as a no-gain null. The operational lesson is unchanged and now ~80 milestones old — the retro's 0/0/0 is a detector-wire gap, not reality — but this cycle added a sharper signal: the .453 fallback meant to close that gap (exp4931) itself blocked, so the fix is not done. Fixing that wire + repairing the fallback's window anchor is the highest-leverage operational work; the research itself ran efficiently on a single correctly-utilized GPU.
